title: O-map/way method-taxa: A sampling method for complete plant taxa inventories
author: André Strauss
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6xbhfin

steps.title: Plan Seasonal Inspection Rounds
steps.instruction: Perform 3 complete seasonal inspection rounds within one year (February/March, May/June, and August/September) in the forest target area, ideally carried out by one person.

substeps.instruction: Equip yourself with an orienteering map or similar quality map (paper or electronic, ideally 1:5,000 scale).
Use additional tools including GPS, compass, and recording devices to ensure every accessible place is screened.

steps.title: Screen Along Accessible Ways
steps.instruction: Conduct an initial screening for new taxa along all accessible ways in the target area.

substeps.instruction: Record taxa by direct determination or later via photo and/or plant material.
Record localization using GPS and optionally by sketching on the orienteering map.

Observe maximum recording distances from the way: 3 m for herbaceous plants, 10 m for shrubs (at least 1 m high), and 20 m for trees (at least 2 m high), including all taxa clearly recognizable from the way.
Sketch the inspection track on the orienteering map.

steps.title: Screen Accessible Subareas
steps.instruction: Conduct a second screening for new taxa by meandering in the accessible subareas between all ways and other lines visible on the map or in nature.

substeps.instruction: Exclude taxa already recorded during the way-screening process.
Record taxa and additional notes using the same method as used for taxa along ways.
